turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, hello Doctor. It's real nice to meet you. Am I, uh, am I sitting in the right place here? Okay, good. 

Um... well, my family actually asked me to come in. It’s really just a bit of a misunderstanding, I think. I hope it's alright to say that. We were down at the fair, and I was giving my talk, you know, about the equipment. And I guess I just got a little... overly enthusiastic? I climbed up onto the tractor to show the crowd this, uh, this 'new pattern' I’d been working on. I was just jerking the controls around a bit to demonstrate how it went, but I suppose it must have looked pretty strange to them. 

People started yelling at me to get down, and... well, to be honest, I feel a bit ashamed because I just couldn't make myself stop doing it right then, even with all the shouting. I really didn't mean to cause a fuss or worry anybody, I promise. I hope that doesn't sound too awful?

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes climbing onto a tractor, jerking the controls in a strange manner, and being unable to stop despite people yelling, indicating disorganized and abnormal motor behavior.

turns.doctor_question: When you were on the tractor at the fair, did it feel like you couldn't stop yourself from doing it, or did it feel like a good idea at the time that made sense to you?
turns.patient_response:
Well, sir... I suppose it was a bit of both, if that's alright to say. 

At the very start, it just seemed like a perfectly fine idea. I was up there, and I just wanted so badly to show them that new pattern I mentioned. It made complete sense to me right then. But then... well, when the yelling started, I knew I was upsetting people, and I felt just terrible about it. I knew I should climb down. But I just kept jerking the controls anyway. 

I really couldn't make myself stop doing it, even with all of them hollering at me. It was like I just had to finish showing them, even though I knew it was causing a scene. It's terribly embarrassing to admit that out loud. I hope you don't think too badly of me for it? I'm usually very well-behaved, I promise you.

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes engaging in inappropriate behavior (climbing a tractor and jerking the controls) and being unable to stop their motor actions despite people yelling at them to stop.

turns.doctor_question: Besides what happened at the fair, have there been other times recently where you've done things impulsively that got you into trouble or that you felt you couldn't stop yourself from doing?
turns.patient_response:
Well, gosh... no, sir. I really don't think so. I mean, I'm a pretty quiet fellow, mostly. I just stick to the farm, you know? 

I... I try very hard to be a good neighbor and not cause any trouble for anybody. That business at the fair, that was just a... a one-off, I'm sure of it. I wouldn't want you to think I go around making a habit of that sort of thing. I haven't been doing anything else out of the ordinary, I promise. I just do my chores and mind my own business. Is... is that what you were asking? I hope I'm answering these questions right for you.

symptom_reasoning.S041: The patient explicitly denies engaging in any other impulsive behaviors that could get him into trouble.
symptom_reasoning.S078: The patient denies any other reckless or out-of-the-ordinary behavior, stating he just does his chores and minds his own business.

turns.doctor_question: Growing up as a child and teenager, did you ever get into trouble at school or with your parents for breaking rules, talking back to authority figures, or doing things you weren't supposed to do?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, goodness no, doctor. No, sir. I was always a very good boy, if I do say so myself. 

My parents, well, they were strict, but they raised me right. I always did my chores, never talked back. I liked school well enough, and the teachers were always real kind to me. I wouldn't ever want to disrespect them or break any rules. I think I'd have died of embarrassment if I ever got sent to the principal's office! 

I was just a quiet kid, mostly kept to myself and helped out around the farm. I hope that's the sort of answer you're looking for? I really have always tried my very best to be polite and respectful to folks in charge.

turns.doctor_question: When you were in school, did your teachers ever mention that you had trouble paying attention, sitting still, or staying focused on your work?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, no sir. Not at all. I always made sure to pay real close attention in class. 

Like I was saying before, I really respected my teachers, so I would just sit quiet at my desk and do my work exactly how they asked us to. I mean, I suppose sometimes a boy's mind might wander a little, maybe thinking about the animals or the chores waiting back home, but... but I never fidgeted or caused a fuss, I promise you that. I was a very good listener. 

I hope that's alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need to hear, doctor. I'm trying my best to be helpful.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient denies having trouble staying focused, stating he paid close attention.
symptom_reasoning.S003: The patient explicitly states he was a 'very good listener', denying listening difficulties.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient states he did his work exactly how the teachers asked, denying difficulty following instructions.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient explicitly states he 'never fidgeted'.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states he would 'sit quiet at my desk', denying leaving his seat inappropriately.

turns.doctor_question: In the weeks or months before the incident at the fair, did you notice any changes in your mood or energy level? For example, did you feel unusually happy, excited, or full of energy for several days at a time?
turns.patient_response:
Well, gosh, doctor... I'm not sure if it was exactly like that. I mean, I wouldn't say I was acting strange or anything. I've just been... feeling pretty good lately, you know? 

I guess... well, some mornings I'd wake up and just feel like the whole valley was opening up for me. I'd be out there doing my chores, grinning at nothing at all, just feeling real pleased with the world. I hope that's normal enough? I mean, a man's allowed to enjoy a nice morning on his farm, isn't he? 

But... well, I suppose I have been a little... short with folks, maybe. Just a bit. Like, if one of the hired hands questions how I'm doing something, or if my wife tells me I need to slow down and rest... I don't know, I just snap at them. It feels like they've insulted the family name or something, and I just get so fired up. I don't mean to be rude, really I don't. I always apologize after. I'm usually a very patient man, I promise. Do you think that's what you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient describes periods of feeling unusually good and 'grinning at nothing,' as well as getting easily 'fired up' and snapping at others, indicating both elevated and irritable mood.
symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient admits to reacting sharply to minor stimuli, such as snapping at hired hands or his wife when they question him or suggest he rest.

turns.doctor_question: When you wake up feeling that way—like the whole valley is opening up for you and you're grinning at nothing—how many days in a row does that feeling usually last before it goes away?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doctor, I... I suppose it lasts a fair bit. I don't want you to think I'm just running wild out there, neglecting my duties or anything. I'm still working hard, harder than ever, really. 

But, um... if I'm being completely honest, and I know you need me to be... those stretches where I'm just buzzing with energy, not needing much sleep, just going and going... well, I'd say they've taken up about ten months out of this past year or so. 

Is that... is that an alright answer? I mean, I know it sounds like a long time to be so fired up, but I promise I've been getting a lot done around the farm. I haven't been slacking off. I just hope I'm not giving you a bad impression of me.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient confirms experiencing long stretches of being 'fired up' and 'buzzing with energy', corresponding to the elevated mood the doctor asked about.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient describes being 'buzzing with energy' and 'just going and going'.
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly states they are 'not needing much sleep' during these stretches.
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient notes they are 'working hard, harder than ever' and 'getting a lot done around the farm', indicating increased goal-directed activity.

turns.doctor_question: During those times when you're not feeling that buzzing energy and good mood—have you had periods where you felt quite down, sad, or depressed? If so, how long would those low periods typically last?
turns.patient_response:
Well, no, sir. I wouldn't say I get sad or depressed. I mean, I'm a pretty steady fellow, usually. 

I suppose sometimes, after a long stretch of working real hard, a man might just feel a bit... tired, you know? Just worn out from the chores and the weather. But I wouldn't call it depression, not at all. I don't lay about in bed all day weeping or anything unseemly like that. I always make sure to pull my weight and provide for my family. 

I might have a quiet day here or there where I don't have much to say, but that's just normal for a man my age, isn't it? I hope that makes sense, doctor. I just want to assure you I'm not the sort to let myself get all moped up and useless. Does that sound like a reasonable answer to you?

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling sad or depressed, stating he doesn't get 'moped up' or lay in bed weeping.
